record.paper_title: Open Problem: Average-Case Hardness of Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection
record.original_question: For the hypergraphic planted clique detection problem G_d(N, 1/2) versus G_d(N, 1/2, kappa), where a test solves detection when the sum of type-I and type-II errors converges to zero, can the conjectured polynomial-time hardness of HPC detection below the kappa on the order of sqrt(N) regime be supported for additional classes of algorithms, specifically statistical query algorithms, sum-of-squares algorithms, belief propagation, approximate message passing, or other algorithmic models beyond the already cited evidence from Metropolis algorithms and low-degree polynomial algorithms?

evidence.quote: more evidence for HPC detection conjecture under more classes

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has provided partial evidence for the conjecture under additional restricted models. In particular, low-degree polynomial lower bounds for hypergraph planted-subgraph/clique-type problems have been extended (e.g., low-degree security of planted random subgraph extending to hypergraphs, 2024), and nearly tight sum-of-squares lower bounds are known for the graph planted clique. However, a comprehensive set of matching hardness results for HPC detection across statistical query, sum-of-squares, belief propagation, and AMP algorithms at the $\sqrt{N}$ threshold has not been fully established, so the problem remains only partially resolved.

The Erdős–Rényi $d$-uniform random hypergraph $G_d(N,1/2)$ has vertex set $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ and each of the $\binom{N}{d}$ possible $d$-element hyperedges is included independently with probability $1/2$. The planted model $G_d(N,1/2,\kappa)$ is obtained by first sampling $G_d(N,1/2)$, then choosing a uniformly random subset $K\subseteq[N]$ with $|K|=\kappa$ and adding every $d$-element subset of $K$ as a hyperedge (so $K$ becomes a hypergraphic clique).

The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem asks, given a single sample, to distinguish
$$H_0:\ G\sim G_d(N,1/2)\quad\text{versus}\quad H_1:\ G\sim G_d(N,1/2,\kappa).$$
A (possibly randomized) test $\psi:\{\text{hypergraphs on }[N]\}\to\{0,1\}$ is said to solve detection asymptotically if
$$\mathbb{P}_{H_0}[\psi=1]+\mathbb{P}_{H_1}[\psi=0]\longrightarrow 0\quad\text{as }N\to\infty.$$
It is conjectured that, for any fixed $d\ge 3$ and any $\kappa=\kappa(N)$ with $\kappa\le N^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, no polynomial-time test solves HPC detection.

Problem. Provide rigorous evidence for this conjectured computational hardness within additional restricted models of computation beyond Metropolis-type algorithms and low-degree polynomial tests. (a) statistical query algorithms (with an appropriate query and tolerance model for hypergraph distributions);
(b) the sum-of-squares hierarchy, by exhibiting pseudo-expectations of degree growing with $N$ that certify indistinguishability when $\kappa=o(\sqrt{N})$;
(c) belief propagation on the associated factor graph;
